profile.headline: Systems Engineer & Town Government Participant
profile.summary:
I have over 10 years experience in high-tech fields (from technical support to web development) and customer relations (ranging from phone service to face-to-face interactions at private homes & client sites).

Due to my inherently investigative and enterprising nature, I have strong analytical skills, the ability to diagnose & solve complex problems, strong communication skills, and I can work alone or as part of a team.

Between my military experience (from which I have an Honorable Discharge) and one of my volunteer positions (as a committee chairman in my local government), I can additionally offer an employer leadership skills. However, because of that background, I also understand the importance of working with existing procedures & personnel.

I am considering work in Systems Engineering, Knowledgebase Management, Technical Support, IT/IS, Quality Engineering, as well as positions in the burgeoning cannabis marketplace.

-----

Specialties:
 - Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, goal-oriented, and ability to work with minimal supervision 
- Ability to diagnose and solve complex problems as well as produce innovative proposals/solutions 
- Technical writing and editing
- Experience using CRM packages and Knowledgebase tools
- Strong interpersonal skills; effective communication at all levels within a company and with outside contacts

positions.title: Town Meeting Member
positions.description:
I am an elected local representative for the residents of Precinct 3 in Milford, MA. This is a volunteer position that usually meets twice per year to approve/review a variety of Town business.  Duties have also included occasional public speaking and familiarity with Robert's Rules of Order.

[Milford is a town of 25K-30K people, organized into 8 precincts and represented at Town Meeting by 240 elected residents (like me).  Overall Town budgets have been over $80M for several years now, and the Town's total assessed valuation is over $3B (FY'10)... to help with comparison to a corporate enterprise.]

I hold a seat that is up for public election every 3 years, and I'm now in my fifth term (after filling a vacancy and some redistricting).

positions.title: Participating Member
positions.description:
Associate Member (from Precinct 3) of the Town Meeting Study & Improvement Committee [TMSIC], a standing committee of the Town Meeting of Milford, MA.  [Full Membership has statutory constraints, so the TMSIC expanded the rolls of Participating Members & Consultants.]  

The main mission of the committee is to study best-practices and promote application of changes that could improve how our Town Meeting conducts its business.  Based on survey results (from the Town Meeting Members), the TMSIC has already enacted several changes to the Town Meeting procedures.

positions.title: Chairman, Capital Improvement Committee
positions.description:
The CIC is an appointed body with 5 volunteer members (including me).  For over 2 decades, this board has approved/reviewed all Town capital expenditures over $20K or those involving Town-owned vehicles/properties, and then advised Town Meeting and the Town's Finance Committee.

Repeatedly appointed to review the Town’s capital requests, prioritize those expenditures, design & maintain a tracking database of those capital improvements, generate written reports, and then make oral presentations to the Town's Finance Committee and Town Meeting.  As chairman, I set agendas & moderate public meetings, oversee the membership & staff, file financial documents & other official communications, and have also hired support staff.  Furthermore, I act as the committee’s liaison to several Town departments, boards, commissions, and committees.

[Overall Town budgets have been over $80M for several years now, and the Town's total assessed valuation is over $3B (FY'10).  Although I am one member of one part of the Town's financial team, I am a committee officer, and during my term, Town finances have remained relatively strong... without need for tax overrides, debt-limit increases, nor outright capital freezes.]

While I was officially appointed (and took my oath of office) in June 2009, I was actually nominated (nonbinding) for membership by this board in December 2007.

After nearly a year as a member of this body, I was elected to the Vice-Chair by my peers at our meeting on 10 May 2010... this position was reaffirmed at the Committee meeting on 4 March 2011.

On 8/29/2011, I was nominated to and voted-in as the Chairman of the CIC, which has been reaffirmed every year since.

positions.title: Computer Engineer/Web Developer/Sole-Proprietor
positions.description:
[key'-ops guild]

I have performed a variety of technical duties, including software production, electronics manufacturing & quality control, software & hardware support (by phone & at deskside/client sites), PC repair & upgrades, technical writing, pre-sales support, technical training, database design, database management, Internet security, and software & web development.

Some of my more well-known clients have included:  Geek Squad/Best Buy, Block Financial Corp. (div. of H&R Block); Polaroid; Harvard Pilgrim Healthcare; Lotus Development Corp.; Cossor Electronics, Ltd. (U.K. div. of Raytheon); and SummerTech (Columbus [OH] Public School System).

Hardcopy references available upon request.

positions.title: Personal Caregiver for Cancer Patient
positions.description:
Provided round-the-clock support for child with leukemia [A.L.L.], who was undergoing radiation & chemotherapy.  Duties have included:  bed-side attendance (in-home & at hospital), regular checking of vital statistics, providing proper nutrition (according to dietary plans), administering IV & oral drugs (the former manually & by programmable pumps -- everything from toxic chemotherapies down to harmless fluoride supplements), de-accessing port-a-caths, proper disposal of medical waste, maintaining medical records, basic on-line medical research, interfacing with medical staff (both in-home & at clinics/labs), posting regular health updates (to a specialized on-line community), and transportation to/from medical facilities.

After achieving the 5-year milestone from my youngest son's diagnosis in February 2011 (and since his active treatment ended in March of 2008), my extra duties are no longer required.  However, I will continue to provide support as needed during clinic visits... currently, once every year (baring any emergencies) for the foreseeable future.

Additionally, as my son was the recipient of blood products during his active treatment, I also continue to regularly donate blood or blood products, when appropriate... I'm a member of the Gallon+ Club at Children's Hospital (Boston), as well as being on the National Bone Marrow Registry.

positions.title: Enumerator
positions.description:
On my last assignment [CCM-PI], I was an interviewer with the Census Coverage Measurement team.  Our overall mission was to determine the level of accuracy of the 2010 Census. Duties included some traveling to conduct personal & confidential interviews from a preselected sample of households in my local region.

Initially, I performed address canvassing (in 3 different phases [AC, GQV, & CCM-IHUFU], over approximately one year)... basically, in order to make sure we included everyone in the 2010 Census, we resolved address conflicts and verified that there really were housing units where we thought they were.  Duties also included conducting personal & confidential interviews, attention to clerical details, geospotting, and strong map-reading abilities.

Regardless the Census phase, my work schedule was mostly independent with (semi)regular team meetings.  And, while various Census activities continue from time to time, my temporary contract ended with the CCM-PI phase in Fall 2010; although, it is possible that I could be called back for related assignments in the future.

Coincidentally, one of my old contract jobs was to use Census data in combination with ZIP Code maps [a.k.a., GIS], so it looks like I'm going full circle with this one. 

Hardcopy reference also available upon request.

company.name: US Department of Commerce, Census Bureau

positions.title: Web Developer (contractor)
positions.description:
Webmaster/Web Developer for H&R Block's TaxCut software; also maintained the websites of a few legacy Block software products. Duties included posting/removing website files (on a secured web host), Web Development (using Java, JavaScript, & HTML), software version control, maintenance of existing software assets, and liaising with other contractors & Block management.

Mostly day-time office work (occasional off-shift work or at-home duties) with some out-of-state travel.  Contract ended with the tax season.

positions.title: Systems Engineer; Knowledgebase Coordinator
positions.description:
As a Systems Engineer, I provided high quality technical support for customers of Elron's network security/management products:  Firewall, Internet Manager, Message Inspector,  Bandwidth Optimizer/Analyzer, SofTrack, and Year2000 Scan & Fix.  Responsibilities included familiarity with the 7 OSI Layers, standard networking practices, various Internet protocols, content filtering, and Internet security.

As Knowledgebase Coordinator, I was responsible for the technical content & look-and-feel of all our knowledgebases.  Also, I wrote over 35 technotes and edited countless others.

positions.title: Technical Support (contractor)
positions.description:
[Principle client was Polaroid (Waltham & Dedham, MA).]

Temporary IT work, before starting full-time employment. I provided consistently high quality technical support for users of all of Polaroid's desktop applications. Also, performed setup and troubleshooting for TCP/IP & Novell NetWare clients. Duties also included installing/upgrading various computer hardware, such as memory modules, expansion cards, disk drives, and peripherals.

positions.title: Technical Support Engineer
positions.description:
I provided consistently high quality technical support for customers of Rational's Automated Software Quality products:  LoadTest, TeamTest, and VisualTest.

I also authored several technotes & FAQs.  And, I worked with the Web Team to improve the quality & consistency of the support-related offerings on our website and FTP sites.

Hardcopy customer reference available upon request.

positions.title: Technical Support (contractor)
positions.description:
[Principle client was Harvard Pilgrim Heathcare (Waltham & Lexington, MA).]

Temporary IT work, before starting full-time employment.  I provided consistently high quality technical support for users of all of HPHC's desktop applications: 1-2-3, cc:Mail, Notes, On-Time, Meeting Maker, WordPerfect, MS Office, Reflection 1 & 2, Chameleon Suite, Netscape, and Norton Anti-virus.  Also, performed setup and troubleshooting for TCP/IP & Novell NetWare clients.  Duties also included installing/upgrading various computer hardware, such as memory modules, expansion cards, disk drives, and peripherals.

positions.title: Quality Engineering; Sr. Technical Support Analyst
positions.description:
In my last position with Quality Engineering, I performed smoke testing of Lotus Components under Windows 95/NT.  Duties included following existing test plans, reporting/tracking software defects, and familiarity with Lotus Notes.

As a Senior Technical Support Analyst, I provided consistently high quality technical support for customers of Lotus' desktop products:  1-2-3, Approach, Freelance Graphics, and common tools.  Responsibilities included being the Product Point Person for 1-2-3 & Freelance Graphics (basically a liaison between our 2nd tier and 1st tier product support centers); also, I was 1 of only 3 TSANet contacts for Lotus' desktop products.  Other responsibilities included representing the 1-2-3 Product Focus Group at departmental meetings and presenting overviews of the 1-2-3 team's efforts.

While I was in Desktop Technical Support, I authored over 80 technotes (at least one of which was in the Top 3 requests by automated support customers) and 165 technical update reports (more TURs than anyone else -- resulted in being listed as Contributor to over 75 existing technotes).  Also, represented Desktop Technical Support on the Orion Project Team, which was tasked with improving the Lotus knowledgebase system.

Additionally, I provided technical training, for internal colleagues and external students.  Duties included creating and presenting an internal training for Freelance Graphics 96 (just prior to product rollout).  Also, I was an Assistant Trainer for 1-2-3 & Freelance Graphics for Lotus Nonprofit Training & L.A.R.E.

Hardcopy references (from management & customers) available upon request.

positions.title: Telecommunications Terminal Devices Repair; Specialist
positions.description:
Received my Honorable Discharge in July 1999. [The same week as the birth of my first son.]

Member of two units, responsible for Telecommunications Terminal Devices Repair [29J].  At both duty stations, I was a Team Leader in their electronics maintenance shops.  Technical duties included installing operating systems, applications, and updates (DOS & UNIX systems).  Also, performed preventive maintenance, upgrades, troubleshooting, and service (from field to depot) on the telecommunications devices & networks controlled by my units.

As a Specialist, I was a Squad Leader, in charge of daily troop accountability & inspections, plus occassional work details.  I was also an Assistant Platoon Guide, in charge of platoon accountability and company reports.  Additionally, I evaluated troop proficiency during training exercises (including NBC survivability).

On my last drill, I was offered promotion to full NCO... since I already had the time-in-grade, promotion points, pre-requisite leadership training, and Sergeant slot (as a squad leader), that was just a formality... still, it's always nice to be wanted, when you're leaving the party.  
[I keep a copy of that promotions list, right next to my discharge certificate.]

positions.title: Database Manager/Programmer; IT; Customer Service; Logistics (contractor)
positions.description:
Managed ZIP-Code-centric databases in MS FoxPro, programmed scripts to process Census data, produced & shipped databases (nationally, on media ranging from CDs to computer reels), provided deskside IT service (for small, networked office), responsible for customer phone support, and provided logistical support during moves/remodels.

Temporary contract work for startup company, mostly daytime office work with occasional third-shift solo work.

positions.title: Quality Control; Electronics Manufacturing (contractor)
positions.description:
[Principle client was Design Circuits, Inc. (Southborough, MA).]

Temporary electronics manufacturing work, before starting full-time job with previous client.  Initial responsibilities included microelectronics assembly, soldering (by hand & wave process), and shipping.  After advancing to Quality Control, duties shifted to testing, rework, and inspection of PCBs.

[Provided as a potential networking resource only.]

positions.title: Quality Control; Software Production (contractor)
positions.description:
[Principle client was Lotus Development Corp. (Cambridge & North Reading, MA).]

Temporary software production work, before starting full-time job with client. Duties included mass-producing consumer software, labeling media, packaging, recycling/destroying rejected media, and Quality Control.

[Provided as a potential networking resource only.]

positions.title: Software Engineer; Test Engineer
positions.description:
[A Raytheon Subcontractor, FAA's TDWR Project]

As a Test Engineer, I created digital signal processor [DSP] interface scripts, used in system tests and excuted by the software I had worked on previously.

As a Software Engineer, I was the member of a small software team who was responsible for design, development, & documentation of a hardware interface simulator, compliant with DoD-Std-2167A.  Duties included requirements analysis/tracking, software design, porting old (FORTRAN) code to new (UNIX) systems, reverse-engineering old (Assembly Language) routines, computer programming (in FORTRAN), software testing, version control, software integration, and technical writing.  Additionally, presented preliminary design to FAA review conference; my entire design was approved without action items.

Also, when I was a Software Engineer, my immediate software team won an award "For Excellence in Design" (from client, Raytheon). Overall project team also earned praise (again from Raytheon) for successful completion of design reviews (by ultimate customer, FAA).  Hardcopies of both are available upon request.

positions.title: Engineering Intern
positions.description:
[A Raytheon Company]

Member of an engineering support team (AvSat Project); I was responsible for prototyping a satellite-based ground-air communications simulator (based on the Viterbi decoding algorithm). Duties included software design, computer programming (in Pascal), software testing, technical research, and technical writing.

Hardcopy references (from management & internship program) available upon request.

positions.title: Engineering Support
positions.description:
Provided engineering support and clerical assistance for a small civil/environmental engineering consulting firm.  Duties included technical support (deskside IT & customer phone service), computer programming, dBase management, spreedsheet design, data entry, civil drafting, blueprinting, proofreading, word processing (technical & legal), VAR marketing, pre-sales technical demonstrations (at prospect offices), customer service, and payroll.

Mostly office work with some travel to municipal clients & commercial prospects across New England.

positions.title: Kitchen Assistant
positions.description:
Temporary food service work (mainly dishwashing), before returning to school full-time.

[Provided as a potential networking resource only.]

positions.title: Support Volunteer, Summer Tech '84
positions.description: Volunteer Teaching Assistant for a computer-centric continuing education program, Summer Tech '84. Duties included assisting teachers/students (in class & labs), computer programming (in BASIC), and deskside technical support.

positions.title: Support Volunteer, Summer Tech '83
positions.description: Volunteer Teaching/Staff Assistant for a computer-centric continuing education program, Summer Tech '83. Duties included assisting teachers/students (in class & labs), computer programming (in BASIC), deskside technical support, and logistical support (from program setup to breakdown).

positions.title: Town Meeting Member
positions.description:
I am an elected local representative for the residents of Precinct 3 in Milford, MA. This is a volunteer position that usually meets twice per year to approve/review a variety of Town business.  Duties have also included occasional public speaking and familiarity with Robert's Rules of Order.

[Milford is a town of 25K-30K people, organized into 8 precincts and represented at Town Meeting by 240 elected residents (like me).  Overall Town budgets have been over $80M for several years now, and the Town's total assessed valuation is over $3B (FY'10)... to help with comparison to a corporate enterprise.]

I hold a seat that is up for public election every 3 years, and I'm now in my fifth term (after filling a vacancy and some redistricting).

positions.title: Participating Member
positions.description:
Associate Member (from Precinct 3) of the Town Meeting Study & Improvement Committee [TMSIC], a standing committee of the Town Meeting of Milford, MA.  [Full Membership has statutory constraints, so the TMSIC expanded the rolls of Participating Members & Consultants.]  

The main mission of the committee is to study best-practices and promote application of changes that could improve how our Town Meeting conducts its business.  Based on survey results (from the Town Meeting Members), the TMSIC has already enacted several changes to the Town Meeting procedures.

positions.title: Chairman, Capital Improvement Committee
positions.description:
The CIC is an appointed body with 5 volunteer members (including me).  For over 2 decades, this board has approved/reviewed all Town capital expenditures over $20K or those involving Town-owned vehicles/properties, and then advised Town Meeting and the Town's Finance Committee.

Repeatedly appointed to review the Town’s capital requests, prioritize those expenditures, design & maintain a tracking database of those capital improvements, generate written reports, and then make oral presentations to the Town's Finance Committee and Town Meeting.  As chairman, I set agendas & moderate public meetings, oversee the membership & staff, file financial documents & other official communications, and have also hired support staff.  Furthermore, I act as the committee’s liaison to several Town departments, boards, commissions, and committees.

[Overall Town budgets have been over $80M for several years now, and the Town's total assessed valuation is over $3B (FY'10).  Although I am one member of one part of the Town's financial team, I am a committee officer, and during my term, Town finances have remained relatively strong... without need for tax overrides, debt-limit increases, nor outright capital freezes.]

While I was officially appointed (and took my oath of office) in June 2009, I was actually nominated (nonbinding) for membership by this board in December 2007.

After nearly a year as a member of this body, I was elected to the Vice-Chair by my peers at our meeting on 10 May 2010... this position was reaffirmed at the Committee meeting on 4 March 2011.

On 8/29/2011, I was nominated to and voted-in as the Chairman of the CIC, which has been reaffirmed every year since.

experience.title: Personal Caregiver for Cancer Patient
experience.description:
Provided round-the-clock support for child with leukemia [A.L.L.], who was undergoing radiation & chemotherapy.  Duties have included:  bed-side attendance (in-home & at hospital), regular checking of vital statistics, providing proper nutrition (according to dietary plans), administering IV & oral drugs (the former manually & by programmable pumps -- everything from toxic chemotherapies down to harmless fluoride supplements), de-accessing port-a-caths, proper disposal of medical waste, maintaining medical records, basic on-line medical research, interfacing with medical staff (both in-home & at clinics/labs), posting regular health updates (to a specialized on-line community), and transportation to/from medical facilities.

After achieving the 5-year milestone from my youngest son's diagnosis in February 2011 (and since his active treatment ended in March of 2008), my extra duties are no longer required.  However, I will continue to provide support as needed during clinic visits... currently, once every year (baring any emergencies) for the foreseeable future.

Additionally, as my son was the recipient of blood products during his active treatment, I also continue to regularly donate blood or blood products, when appropriate... I'm a member of the Gallon+ Club at Children's Hospital (Boston), as well as being on the National Bone Marrow Registry.

experience.title: Enumerator
experience.description:
On my last assignment [CCM-PI], I was an interviewer with the Census Coverage Measurement team.  Our overall mission was to determine the level of accuracy of the 2010 Census. Duties included some traveling to conduct personal & confidential interviews from a preselected sample of households in my local region.

Initially, I performed address canvassing (in 3 different phases [AC, GQV, & CCM-IHUFU], over approximately one year)... basically, in order to make sure we included everyone in the 2010 Census, we resolved address conflicts and verified that there really were housing units where we thought they were.  Duties also included conducting personal & confidential interviews, attention to clerical details, geospotting, and strong map-reading abilities.

Regardless the Census phase, my work schedule was mostly independent with (semi)regular team meetings.  And, while various Census activities continue from time to time, my temporary contract ended with the CCM-PI phase in Fall 2010; although, it is possible that I could be called back for related assignments in the future.

Coincidentally, one of my old contract jobs was to use Census data in combination with ZIP Code maps [a.k.a., GIS], so it looks like I'm going full circle with this one. 

Hardcopy reference also available upon request.
